subject: Reserved commit term + start-date flexibility discussion — HorizonWorks
messages:
From: Aileen Cho <aileen@horizonworks.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Berg <markus.berg@horizonworks.com>, procurement@horizonworks.com
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved commit options and possible delayed pool start

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency/throughput numbers looked promising. Procurement pinged me this morning: we need to formalize reserved commit options (12/24/36 months) and understand tradeoffs if we need to push the capacity start date out a few weeks. Two constraints on our side:

- Our legal team prefers a 30–45 day procurement window after signing (so start date may be delayed).
- We have tuning work to finalize model quantization and an infra runbook; this means we may not want the GPUs fully provisioned until that work is done.

High level numbers from our side (attached spreadsheet): expected sustained usage ~2.1M tokens/day, peak bursts ~9–12k tokens/sec for short windows. We're evaluating a dedicated pool sized for ~3x our steady-state to cover peaks.

Questions:
1) Can Redwood provide term-tiered discounts for 12/24/36-month reserved commits?
2) If the start date slips beyond 30 days, are there credits or a deferred-start mechanism so we don't pay full price while onboarding?
3) What throughput guarantees or remediation (credits/extra capacity) do you provide if the provisioned pool underperforms during peak ramp?

If you can send a term sheet with options and a proposed ramp schedule (including a staging/burst buffer), I can take it to procurement later this week.

Best,
Aileen
Director of AI Engineering
HorizonWorks

Attachment: HorizonWorks_Projected_Usage.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Aileen Cho <aileen@horizonworks.com>
Cc: dev_patel <dev@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved commit options and possible delayed pool start

Hi Aileen — thanks for the clear ask and the spreadsheet (received). Attached is a concise term sheet that outlines our standard reserved-commit structure and a few deferred-start options. Summary here so procurement has quick bullets: 

- Term / list discount (off hosted single-tenant baseline): 12 months = 8%
  24 months = 14%
  36 months = 20%

- Deferred-start options:
  a) 30-day free staging window after signature (no billing for inactive pool; pool reserved but scaled to 0.1x compute).
  b) Deferred-billing credit: if start >30 days and <= 90 days, we apply a one-time onboarding credit equal to 15% of month-1 invoice.
  c) If customer requests explicit guaranteed hold (no provision) beyond 90 days, we require a minimum 3-month ramp commitment or an increase in the minimum monthly commit to preserve capacity—details negotiable.

- Throughput guarantees: for Dedicated pools we offer a throughput SLO tied to the provisioned vGPU count. Remedy for not meeting SLO: service credit up to 20% of monthly commit for the impacted window OR temporary burst allocation for the same billing period (whichever the customer prefers). SLOs and exact numbers are specified per-pool in the term sheet.

- GPU sizing guidance: based on your projected peaks, we'd recommend a baseline pool of 8 A100-equivalent slots with a 2x burst buffer (autoscale) to cover peak windows — this maps to the committed qps/tokens in the attached term sheet. Marcus and Dev are cc'd for follow-up on sizing and staging.

I've attached ReservedCommit_TermSheet_v2.pdf with a sample ramp schedule: 0–30 days: staging and onboarding (0.1x active), 31–90 days: 50% active, 91–180 days: full active. We can adjust the ramp slope if you need faster or slower activation.

If procurement is ready, we can run a parallel DocuSign workflow that includes the deferred-start addendum. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call to walk procurement through the credit mechanics.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Account Exec, Dedicated Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachment: ReservedCommit_TermSheet_v2.pdf

From: dev_patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 09:00:00 -07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: sizing note for HorizonWorks

Kimberly / Marcus — quick internal note before we lock numbers:

- The spreadsheet looks like steady-state at ~2.1M tokens/day with 12k tokens/sec peaks. If HorizonWorks quantizes aggressively (8-bit), the same throughput maps to ~30–40% fewer vGPU-hours. Recommend we offer two pricing profiles in the term sheet: "as-is" (no quantization) and "quantized" (assumes customer will run our verified 8-bit path).
- For deferred start we should offer a one-time free burst allocation (2 A100-eq for up to 72 hours) to validate peak runs without incurring full-month charges. That reduces friction for early performance tests.
- Operational note: add a clause that allows a single one-time pool resize within the first 120 days without penalty to accommodate measurement drift.

I'll be on the call if they want a quick technical walkthrough.

- Dev

From: Markus Berg <markus.berg@horizonworks.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Aileen Cho <aileen@horizonworks.com>, procurement@horizonworks.com
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 10:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved commit options and possible delayed pool start

Kimberly,

Appreciate the clarity — the tiered discounts make sense. Procurement prefers the deferred-billing credit (option b) over a free staging window. Two quick asks before we get legal involved:

1) Can you commit to the one-time free burst allocation Dev mentioned (2x A100-eq for up to 72 hours) for performance validation?
2) We'd like DocuSign to include the deferred-start addendum as a checkbox so our legal doesn't have to handle multiple amendments.

If you can confirm those two pieces, I'll route the term sheet to legal and procurement today. We are leaning toward 24 months but want the start-date flexibility baked in.

Thanks,
Markus
CTO, HorizonWorks
